### The Path to Short-Lived Greatness
Author: Jon Bloom
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/the-path-to-short-lived-greatness
Passage: Matthew 23:11
Points:
- Secular and religious meritocracies define greatness through worldly status and human applause.
- The Pharisees fell into spiritual corruption because their primary motive was to be seen by people.
- Jesus redefined greatness by commanding His followers to pursue the humble posture of a servant.
- Believers can freely set aside self-exaltation because they rely on God's grace and His eternal reward.

### Do You Relate to the Pharisees?
Author: Adrian Rogers
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/loveworthfinding/love-worth-finding-october-21-2022.html
Passage: Matthew 23:23
Points:
- Religious legalism can fill a person's head with Scripture while leaving the heart full of sin.
- Meticulous rule-following easily blinds believers to weightier spiritual matters like justice and mercy.
- Scripture is meant to be a life-giving guide rather than a weapon used to judge and beat others down.
- True devotion requires walking in genuine Christlike love rather than relying on empty religious observance.

### I Would Have Made a Great Pharisee
Author: Glynnis Whitwer
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement/encouragement-for-today-september-13-2011.html
Passage: Matthew 23:25
Points:
- Focusing purely on external rules creates a false sense of security while ignoring inner spiritual decay.
- God frequently uses stressful circumstances to expose hidden pride, bitterness, and insecurity in the heart.
- Cleansing the inside of the cup requires admitting our faults instead of maintaining a righteous facade.
- Real discipleship means choosing humble intimacy with Jesus over superficial religious performance.

### Bible Pathways - Oct. 10, 2008
Author: Bible Pathway Ministries
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathways-oct-10-2008-11582783.html
Passage: Matthew 23:1-36
Points:
- Jesus directly confronted the scribes and Pharisees for their pride, legalism, and desire for public praise.
- Religious leaders blinded themselves by obsessing over outward rituals while ignoring God's truth.
- External appearances of piety cannot conceal inward hypocrisy and lawlessness from God's sight.
- Believers must evaluate their own hearts to ensure they are not trading true faith for worldly prestige.
